svg.aria-label: The Raspberry Pi 5 forty-pin GPIO header drawn top-down, with each pin numbered one through forty and labelled with its standard function. Pin two and pin four are highlighted red as the five-volt power pins. Pins six, nine, fourteen, twenty, twenty-five, thirty, thirty-four, and thirty-nine are highlighted black as ground pins. All other pins are drawn in neutral grey.
svg.title: D-4.1 — Pi 5 40-pin GPIO header with 5 V and GND pins highlighted
svg.desc: Top-down view of the Raspberry Pi 5 forty-pin GPIO header. Pin 1 is in the top-left corner. Odd pins run along the top row left to right; even pins run along the bottom row left to right. Each pin is drawn as a small numbered square with its standard function written above (odd row) or below (even row). 5 V pins (2 and 4) are filled in red. Ground pins (6, 9, 14, 20, 25, 30, 34, 39) are filled in black. All other pins are neutral grey.
svg.text: Pin 1 is in the corner nearest the SD-card slot. Odd pins on the top row; even pins on the bottom row. We need pin 2 (red) and pin 6 (black) for this chapter.

g.text: Pin 1 is at the top-left of this corner.
Use these two pins in Chapter 4
Odd pins (1, 3, 5, …) run along the top row.
Even pins (2, 4, 6, …) run along the bottom row.
Pin 1 is in the corner closest to the SD-card slot;
pin 40 is at the opposite end of the header.
